reading.p: This lesson explains the Sacrament of Penance: what it is, why we need it, its purpose, why we practice it before Holy Communion, its biblical authority, how it works, how to prepare for it, which sins can be forgiven, and what blasphemy against the Holy Spirit means.

reading.h2: What Is the Sacrament of Penance?

reading.p: Penance is a sacred sacrament through which a baptized believer who has fallen into sin returns to God by sincerely repenting, confessing their sins to a priest, and receiving absolution through the grace of the Holy Spirit.
Penance has three components that work together: Repentance, which is the heart's return; Confession, which is the verbal act; and Absolution, which is God's forgiveness given through a priest.
Sin separates us from God. From the very beginning, sin created separation. In Genesis 3, when Adam and Eve sinned, they hid from God, which symbolizes the inner distance that sin creates.

reading.quote: Your iniquities have separated you from your God; your sins have hidden His face from you.

reading.p: This shows that sin is not merely breaking rules; it is breaking relationship. Penance is God's remedy for restoring communion with Him.

reading.h2: What Is the Purpose of Penance?

reading.p: Penance restores our relationship with God. Through true repentance and confession, we are reconciled to Him.

reading.quote: Return to Me, and I will return to you, says the Lord.

reading.p: The Parable of the Prodigal Son (Luke 15:11-32) is the perfect example. The son left his father's house and lived a wrong life, but when he repented and returned, the father ran to him, embraced him, and restored him to full sonship. This is exactly what happens in the Sacrament of Penance: God rejoices when we return.

reading.quote: There will be more joy in heaven over one sinner who repents than over ninety-nine just persons who need no repentance.

reading.h2: Why We Practice Penance Before Holy Communion

reading.p: Penance prepares us to receive Holy Communion worthily. The Eucharist is union with Christ, so we must approach it in a state of grace, not weighed down by unconfessed sin.

reading.quote: Let a man examine himself, and so let him eat of that bread, and drink of that cup. For he who eats and drinks in an unworthy manner eats and drinks judgment to himself, not discerning the Lord's body.

reading.p: This is not a threat but a loving warning: we must not treat Holy Communion lightly.

reading.h2: Biblical Authority: How Christ Instituted Penance

reading.quote: Whatever you bind on earth shall be bound in heaven, and whatever you loose on earth shall be loosed in heaven.

reading.p: Christ spoke this with Peter after Peter confessed that Jesus was the Son of God. "Binding and loosing" was rabbinic language: to bind meant to prohibit or withhold, and to loose meant to permit or forgive. Christ gave the keys of the kingdom of heaven to Peter, along with the authority to forgive sins on earth.

reading.h3: Matthew 18:18 — Authority for All the Apostles

reading.quote: Whatever you bind on earth will be bound in heaven…

reading.p: This was spoken before Jesus' crucifixion and resurrection. Christ was giving the apostles spiritual jurisdiction as His future representatives. The authority was real, but not yet sacramentally empowered, because the Holy Spirit had not yet been fully imparted. This passage reinforces that the authority was not for Peter alone; it is for all the apostles and their successors, the bishops and priests.

reading.quote: Receive the Holy Spirit. If you forgive the sins of any, they are forgiven them; if you retain them, they are retained.

reading.p: This was spoken after the resurrection. Jesus now breathed the Holy Spirit onto the apostles, an act that spiritually empowered them to carry out the authority He had promised earlier. After the Resurrection, by breathing the Holy Spirit onto His apostles, He gave them direct power to forgive sins as His representatives.

list: Decides to change — does not plan to return to sin (Luke 15:11-32).
Confesses to a priest — especially the sins that dominate the soul.
Trusts in God's mercy — like the woman who heard, "Your sins are forgiven" (John 8:11).
Listens and absolves — acting in Christ's name.
Gives spiritual counsel — how to overcome sin.
Speaks words of absolution — the outward sign.
Maintains complete secrecy — the seal of confession is absolute.
May assign spiritual discipline (epitimia) — not as punishment, but as spiritual therapy.

reading.p: People often ask, "Why not confess directly to God?" The answer is that you do confess to God, but through His chosen method. Christ Himself established confession to a priest. The priest is not acting on his own; he is a witness, a guide, and a channel of God's forgiveness, just as a doctor is a channel of healing.

Jesus gave the authority to bind and loose, and to forgive sins, directly to the Twelve Apostles. But He also intended this authority to continue through the Church by the laying on of hands (ordination), which we call Apostolic Succession. That is why only bishops and priests can perform the Sacrament of Penance.

reading.h2: How Do You Prepare for Penance?

reading.quote: Search me, O God, and know my heart.

reading.p: Ask the Holy Spirit to help you see your sins clearly, without excuses or pride.

Use a spiritual mirror, and reflect on the Ten Commandments; the Beatitudes (Matthew 5); your thoughts, words, actions, and what you failed to do; and your relationships, your prayers, and how you treat your body and soul.

Do not generalize by saying, "I've sinned a lot." Instead, name the sins: "I lied," "I judged," "I neglected prayer," and so on. You are not surprising God; you are naming your wounds so that He can heal them.

reading.quote: A broken and contrite heart, O God, You will not despise.

reading.p: There is no need to justify or blame. True repentance simply says, "Lord, have mercy."
All sins, even the worst, can be forgiven.

reading.quote: Though your sins are like scarlet, they shall be white as snow.
Him who comes to Me I will never cast out.

reading.p: Scripture gives us examples: David (murder), Peter (denial), and the adulterous woman (John 8). The only sin Christ says cannot be forgiven is blasphemy against the Holy Spirit (Matthew 12:31). This refers to a hard-hearted, final rejection of God's grace, a refusal to repent at all. It is not that God will not forgive, but that the person refuses to be forgiven. This is what makes it unforgivable.

reading.h2: What Is Blasphemy Against the Holy Spirit?

reading.p: This is not a simple or merely extreme offense, but a deliberate, conscious, and hardened rejection of the Holy Spirit's work, especially His work of bringing repentance and forgiveness.

reading.quote: Therefore I say to you, every sin and blasphemy will be forgiven men, but the blasphemy against the Spirit will not be forgiven.

reading.p: The context is that Jesus had just healed a demon-possessed man, and the Pharisees accused Him of casting out demons by the power of Satan rather than by the Holy Spirit.

reading.quote: It is not that the Spirit is greater than the Son, but that those who blaspheme the Son often do so out of ignorance. But blasphemy against the Spirit is not out of ignorance, but after full knowledge.
reading.cite: St. John Chrysostom, Homilies on Matthew, 41:3

reading.quote: Blasphemy against the Holy Spirit is a deliberate resistance to the known truth and a refusal to accept salvation.
reading.cite: St. Basil the Great, On the Holy Spirit, 29.72

reading.quote: It is a sin against grace itself, and to sin against grace is to place oneself outside the sphere of healing.
reading.cite: St. Athanasius the Great, Letters, Ep. 40

reading.p: It is not a moment of doubt, fear, or spiritual struggle. It is not ordinary sin or even serious sin. It is not anger at God during suffering. All of these can be forgiven through confession and repentance. The Holy Spirit convicts the heart and calls the sinner to repentance; only when this call is fully and finally rejected does no other path to salvation remain.

It is unforgivable because the person refuses the very means of forgiveness. God does not override human free will. If someone persistently and finally resists the Spirit's work of conviction, illumination, repentance, and renewal, then they cut themselves off from salvation.

studyGuide.overview: Penance is the sacrament by which a baptized believer who has sinned returns to God through repentance, confession to a priest, and absolution given by the grace of the Holy Spirit. Christ instituted it by granting His apostles the authority to bind and loose and to forgive sins, an authority continued through the Church by Apostolic Succession.
keyPoints: Penance has three components: repentance (the heart's return), confession (the verbal act), and absolution (God's forgiveness through the priest).
Sin breaks relationship with God, and Penance is God's remedy to restore communion.
We confess before Holy Communion so as to receive the Eucharist worthily and in a state of grace.
Christ instituted the sacrament in Matthew 16:19, Matthew 18:18, and John 20:22-23, empowering the apostles by the Holy Spirit after the Resurrection.
We confess to a priest because Christ established this method; the priest is a witness, guide, and channel of God's forgiveness, like a doctor of the soul.
Epitimia is spiritual therapy and medicine, not punishment.
All sins can be forgiven; the only exception is blasphemy against the Holy Spirit, which is the deliberate, final refusal to repent.
reviewQuestions: What are the three components of the Sacrament of Penance, and what does each one mean?
How does the Parable of the Prodigal Son illustrate the purpose of Penance?
Why do we practice Penance before receiving Holy Communion?
How do Matthew 16:19, Matthew 18:18, and John 20:22-23 together show that Christ instituted Penance and empowered His apostles?
Why do we confess to a priest rather than only directly to God?
What is epitimia, and why is it described as therapy rather than punishment?
What is blasphemy against the Holy Spirit, and why is it the one sin that remains unforgivable?

checks: Penance is presented as a true Sacrament/Mystery in which the priest looses sins by the authority Christ gave (Matthew 16:19; Matthew 18:18; John 20:23), consistent with Orthodox teaching.
Epitimia is correctly described as spiritual medicine and therapy for healing, not as punishment.
The continuation of the apostolic authority through Apostolic Succession (ordination by laying on of hands) for bishops and priests is affirmed.
The seal of confession, the call to genuine contrition, and absolution by the grace of the Holy Spirit all accord with Tewahedo practice.
Patristic citations (Chrysostom, Basil, Athanasius) are reproduced as given in the source and were not altered or invented.
Nothing in the lesson contradicts the Miaphysite confession or introduces Chalcedonian or Filioque language.
